dependencies.instrument: PD 106/2007 Articles 22–24, with Law 3386/2005 Article 77 formally retained by Law 4251/2014 Article 139(2), and supplementary procedures under Law 5226/2025 Articles 13–16 and 28
dependencies.note: Article 28(2) makes PD 106/2007 Articles 22–24 the return-procedure basis and applies compatible Law 5226/2025 rules supplementarily, preserving more favourable PD provisions. The bounded map is: Article 22 sets substantive expulsion/return grounds and protections; Law 4071/2012 Article 42 amended Article 22(8). Article 23 requires written notice stating the competent court or authority, remedy deadline and normally at least one month to depart; Law 5226 Article 13 adds written reasons, remedy information and requested translation within its stated scope. Article 24(1) of the original PD text cross-refers to Law 3386/2005 Article 77 and case ΙΘ of Ministerial Decision 7004/3/40-θ, as amended and in force; this original wording was verified from the official Ministry-hosted Gazette reproduction and its case ΙΘ historical match is recorded at gr-121. Law 4251/2014 Article 139(2) expressly retained Article 77 and PD 106/2007, so the statutory cross-reference is not simply obsolete; the original 2005 delegation is now verified through the historical Gazette reproduction gr-121: effective 1 January 2006, it assigned Article 77 appeal decisions and Article 78 force-majeure suspension decisions to regional general police directors and the directors of the Attica and Thessaloniki Aliens Directorates. An official MFA-hosted compilation at gr-122 reproduces Article 77 text and lists amendments through Law 3907/2011: it states a five-day appeal, a decision within three working days, and suspension of expulsion but not detention. It does not establish post-2011 amendment status or current wording. The presently operative delegated organ after later reorganization or amendment also remains unverified. Law 5226 Article 14(1) distinguishes police-issued returns (five-day appeal, three-working-day decision, suspensive effect of return but not detention) from returns embedded in residence-title refusal/revocation (ten-day application for reconsideration and five-working-day decision); Article 14(3) addresses administrative temporary suspension and provisional judicial protection, and Article 14(6) annulment review. PD 106 Article 24(2) expressly provides a Council of State annulment action against refusal of registration certificates, residence cards and permanent-residence cards, and withdrawal/non-renewal decisions, as well as decisions on the Article 24(1) administrative appeal against expulsion. Article 24(3) concerns suspension of removal in expulsion proceedings; paragraphs (4)–(5) set the review scope and hearing-presence rule, and paragraph (6) addresses legal aid for an expulsion appeal. These expulsion-specific protections are not assumed to govern a card-refusal action. Article 15 supplies return-period safeguards. Law 5275/2026 Article 57 was checked: its targeted changes affect Law 5226 Articles 4, 22(4) and 23(4), not Articles 13–16 or 28. This is a statutory map only; reconcile authority, forum, deadline, service, stay and interim relief for each decision type before operational use. No current consolidation, complete later-amendment chain or live practice evidence is accepted. The original Article 24(2) wording was directly reviewed from the National Printing House Gazette; current card-refusal deadline, interim relief, amendments and practice remain open (Monitor review: discovery/eudirective-public-data/GR/free-movement/pd106-article24-2-eu-family-card-refusal-remedy-review-2026-10-26.json, SHA-256 c3f0b48dc3acc4481e9fde7be9a0c0286032fa2cbcf94fb39e20debd8e6634b3). Law 5326/2026 Article 32 was directly reviewed at gr-153: it repeals only Law 3068/2002 Articles 1–5 and does not amend or repeal Article 15(3). Article 32 took effect on 4 August 2026 under Article 111(1). This does not verify other amendments or the current text of Article 15(3) (Monitor review: discovery/eudirective-public-data/GR/free-movement/pd106-article24-2-eu-family-card-refusal-remedy-review-2026-10-26.json, SHA-256 c3f0b48dc3acc4481e9fde7be9a0c0286032fa2cbcf94fb39e20debd8e6634b3). Follow-up to PD 106/2007 Article 24(2): Law 4689/2020 Article 57 replaced Law 3068/2002 Article 15 in full. The replacement places venue rules in paragraph 3 and the appeal-to-Council-of-State rule in paragraph 5; paragraph 9 concerns nationality disputes. PD 106 Article 24(2) itself still names a Council of State annulment action for listed card decisions and cites former Article 15(3) as in force. The relationship, competent forum, deadline, interim relief and filing route for each decision type require human legal review. dependencies.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/1191
dependencies.note: For a public document issued by one EU Member State for presentation to another, first check that it is within Regulation 2016/1191 Article 2: covered documents are exempt from Apostille/legalisation and specified copy/translation formalities are simplified. The multilingual form is optional and only a translation aid. The Regulation excludes third-country-issued documents and does not determine substantive recognition of document contents. The MFA page dated 4 June 2026 describes general Greek authentication/translation routes subject to the Regulation and treaty exceptions; do not apply its general Apostille language to an in-scope EU document. MITOS gr-158 is a dated Special Registry receiving-service reference for Greek citizens’ foreign marriage records; check any stated authentication requirement against Regulation 2016/1191 where applicable. Document-specific route, issuing-country status, receiving Greek authority, recognition rule, remedy and live operation remain open.
evidence: EUR-Lex document information for CELEX 32016R1191 reports the act as in force, with no end date; the page lists the 26 July 2016 basic act and no later consolidated version. Its staged application is complete from 16 February 2019.

Regulation Articles 1–3 define the cross-border Member-State/public-document scope and specified civil-status subject matters; Article 2(3) excludes third-country authority documents and Article 2(4) excludes recognition of the legal effects of document contents.

Articles 4–6 exempt covered documents from legalisation/Apostille and simplify certified-copy/translation formalities. Articles 7–8 provide optional multilingual standard forms for specified document classes as attached translation aids with no autonomous legal value.

The Hellenic MFA page dated 4 June 2026 describes authentication-before-translation and Apostille/consular routes while expressly making them subject to Regulation 2016/1191 and other exceptions; it is general route guidance rather than a document-specific decision.

The bounded scope and Greece crosswalk are recorded in Monitor local-only discovery/eudirective-public-data/GR/civil-status/regulation-2016-1191-greece-crosswalk-2026-10-26.json (SHA-256 b6c05f9554ffe286f33413497a83800597dbb89672db43be75de7f5640be242b).
